title: Painful Rash
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset fever, widespread painful target-like lesions, bullae, epidermal detachment (<10% BSA = SJS, 10-30% = SJS/TEN overlap, >30% = TEN), and mucosal involvement (oral, ocular, genital). Nikolsky sign positive (epidermis sloughs with gentle pressure). Most commonly triggered by medications: sulfa antibiotics, anti-epileptics (lamotrigine, phenytoin, carbamazepine), allopurinol, NSAIDs, within 1-8 weeks of exposure. This is a medical emergency. Immediately discontinue offending drug. Admit to burn ICU. Supportive care: fluid/electrolyte management, wound care, infection prevention, nutritional support, ophthalmology consult. Systemic steroids controversial — not universally recommended. IVIG or cyclosporine may be considered. SCORTEN score for prognosis.
chief_complaint: Fever, widespread painful rash, mucosal involvement
